title: How many CPD units do NSW solicitors need each year?
description: NSW solicitor CPD explained: 10 units a year, the four compulsory fields, activity caps, carry over, pro rata units, exemptions, rectification and audits.
shortAnswer: Solicitors holding a New South Wales practising certificate must complete 10 continuing professional development (CPD) units in each CPD year from April 1 to March 31, including at least one unit in each of four compulsory fields: ethics and professional responsibility, practice management and business skills, professional skills, and substantive law. The duty comes from the Legal Profession Uniform Continuing Professional Development (Solicitors) Rules 2015 and is administered by the Law Society of New South Wales.
keyTakeaways: CPD is a statutory condition on every Australian practising certificate under section 52 of the Legal Profession Uniform Law (NSW), which requires compliance with the Uniform CPD (Solicitors) Rules 2015.
The annual requirement is 10 units, with at least one unit in each compulsory field (Rule 6). Up to 3 units completed between January and March can be carried into the next CPD year.
Some activities are capped under Rule 9: passive audio or video study at 5 units, writing at 5 units, presenting at 5 units, and committee work at 3 units.
Solicitors must keep records and evidence for at least 3 years (Rule 12) and, if audited, produce them within 21 days (Rule 14).
A solicitor who declares non-compliance at renewal and has no exemption must lodge a rectification plan (Rule 15).
regulator: Law Society of New South Wales, under the Legal Profession Uniform Law (NSW)
appliesTo: Solicitors holding a New South Wales practising certificate, including employed, in-house and government solicitors
Solicitors practising overseas who keep a New South Wales practising certificate
Accredited specialists, who also have specialist CPD obligations
Law practices that run in-house CPD or keep CPD records for their solicitors

sections.heading: What CPD must a NSW solicitor complete?

blocks.text: A New South Wales solicitor must complete 10 CPD units every CPD year, with at least one unit in each of four compulsory fields. The [Law Society of New South Wales CPD page](https://www.lawsociety.com.au/practising-law-in-NSW/working-as-a-solicitor-in-NSW/your-practising-certificate/CPD) states that CPD "is a statutory condition imposed on all Australian practising certificates, pursuant to s 52 of the Legal Profession Uniform Law (NSW)", and that the condition requires the holder to comply with the Legal Profession Uniform Continuing Professional Development (Solicitors) Rules 2015.

The CPD year runs from April 1 to March 31. Each practising certificate renewal application asks the solicitor to declare whether they complied with their CPD obligations for the year just ended (Rule 13). Because the rules are Uniform Rules made by the Legal Services Council, the same unit count and fields apply in Victoria and Western Australia; the Victorian position, including the separate rules for barristers, is covered on the page about [Victorian lawyer CPD requirements](/regulations/victoria-lawyer-cpd-requirements).

blocks.title: Currency
blocks.text: This page reflects the Law Society of New South Wales CPD guidance and the Uniform CPD (Solicitors) Rules 2015 as at November 2026. The CPD year that began on April 1, 2026 ends on March 31, 2027.

sections.heading: What are the four compulsory CPD fields?

blocks.text: Rule 6 requires at least one unit in each of ethics and professional responsibility, practice management and business skills, professional skills, and substantive law. The remaining six units can be taken in any field that is relevant to the solicitor's practice needs or professional development.

blocks.text: A solicitor who starts or returns to practice part way through the year completes a reduced number of units, but the compulsory fields still have to be covered within those remaining units (Rule 6.2). Firms that track this in a [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) usually add one column per field so gaps show before March.

sections.heading: Which activities count, and which are capped?

blocks.text: CPD in New South Wales is self-assessed: if an activity extends the solicitor's knowledge and skills in areas relevant to their practice needs or professional development, it can be claimed (Rule 7). The Law Society does not accredit CPD providers, and its suggested wording for providers begins "CPD activities are not accredited by the Law Society".

blocks.text: The cap on recorded material catches many online programs. The Law Society distinguishes web-based programs, which are uncapped because they offer interaction with the material, from private study of audio or visual material, which is passive. Its examples of interaction are breakout room discussion, a chat or question function during a live session, quizzes, tests and polls, and scenarios that require a choice to proceed. A firm building its own e-learning should design in at least one of these features if it wants the hours to count without the 5 unit limit.

sections.heading: Can units be carried over or reduced?

blocks.text: Yes, within limits. A solicitor may carry over a maximum of 3 units from the previous CPD year if those units were completed between January and March, and the units cannot be counted in both years.

Pro rata units apply when a solicitor commences or recommences practice during the year. The Law Society's table requires 10 units for an April start, falling by one unit for each later month to 1 unit for a January start, and none for a February or March start.

Exemptions, in whole or in part, require a written application under Rule 16.3. The listed grounds are illness or disability; the location of the solicitor's legal practice; absence for parenting leave or unemployment; reduced hours because of part-time or casual work; being required to hold a practising certificate while not engaged in legal practice; more than 40 years in practice without practicing as a principal; and hardship or other special circumstances. The location ground is about remoteness limiting access to CPD, not practicing overseas; solicitors overseas can earn units in the jurisdiction where they practice.

sections.heading: What records are required, and what happens at audit?

blocks.text: Solicitors must keep a record of activities and supporting evidence for at least 3 years (Rule 12). The Law Society lists attendance records, receipts, in-house CPD records and emails confirming registration as acceptable evidence, and publishes a Record of CPD activities template.

The Law Society runs an annual audit. A selected solicitor must provide CPD records and evidence within 21 days of the request (Rule 14). A solicitor who declares at renewal that they did not comply, and who is not eligible for an exemption, must submit an online Rectification of non-compliance CPD plan setting out the courses and steps they will take (Rule 15). The general method for assembling evidence is in the guide on [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: How should a law firm build its CPD program around the rules?

blocks.text: Start from the four fields and the caps, then plan the year so every solicitor has the compulsory units booked well before March. A practical calendar puts ethics and practice management sessions early in the CPD year, leaves substantive law updates to follow legislative change, and uses January to March for any top-up units, which also become carry-over eligible.

items: **Tag every session by field.** Record the field and unit value on the attendance certificate so solicitors and auditors do not have to infer it.
**Make online learning interactive.** Polls, questions and scenarios move a session out of the capped audio or visual category.
**Track pro rata starters.** Lateral hires and returning parents have reduced unit counts but still need all four fields.

**Link related obligations.** From July 1, 2026 many law practices also became subject to AML/CTF training duties, covered in the page on [AML/CTF tranche 2 training for lawyers and accountants](/regulations/aml-ctf-tranche-2-lawyers-accountants-training). Those sessions can count as CPD where they meet Rule 7.

blocks.text: Legal teams inside regulated organizations face the same rules as private practitioners. The [professional services industry page](/industries/professional-services) describes how firms connect CPD records to wider competence evidence.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each internal session to a CPD field, a unit value and an activity type before content is written, so caps and compulsory fields are checked at design time rather than at renewal. Attendance and assessment records are then held against the same map, producing a per-solicitor record that can be handed to a Law Society auditor within the 21 day window.

faqs.q: Does the Law Society of NSW accredit CPD courses?
faqs.a: No. CPD in New South Wales is based on self-assessment under Rule 7. The solicitor decides whether an activity extends knowledge and skills relevant to their practice needs or professional development, and claims one unit per hour where it does, subject to the Rule 9 caps.

faqs.q: Do watched recordings count towards NSW CPD?
faqs.a: Yes, but passive viewing is private study of audio or visual material and is capped at 5 units a year. A web-based program that offers interaction, such as live questions, polls, quizzes or decision scenarios, is not capped.

faqs.q: What if a solicitor misses the March 31 deadline?
faqs.a: They must declare non-compliance when renewing. If they are not eligible for an exemption, they must lodge a Rectification of non-compliance CPD plan with the Law Society under Rule 15 and complete the outstanding units as soon as possible.

faqs.q: Do part-time solicitors still need 10 units?
faqs.a: Part-time or casual work is a listed ground for a partial exemption under Rule 16.3, but it is not automatic. The solicitor must apply in writing through the Law Society's online exemption application. Without an approved exemption the full 10 units apply.

factCheck.claim: CPD is a statutory condition on all Australian practising certificates under s 52 of the Legal Profession Uniform Law (NSW), requiring compliance with the Uniform CPD (Solicitors) Rules 2015
The CPD year runs from 1 April to 31 March; compliance is declared at renewal (Rule 13)
10 CPD units each year including at least one in each of ethics and professional responsibility, practice management and business skills, professional skills, and substantive law (Rule 6)
Maximum 3 units may be carried over if completed between January and March

Rule 9 caps: private audio/visual study 5 units; legal article 5 units (1 unit per 1,000 words); presenting 5 units; committee membership 3 units (1 unit per 2 hours); seminars and postgraduate study uncapped
Records and evidence must be kept for at least 3 years (Rule 12); audited solicitors must produce records within 21 days (Rule 14)

Exemption grounds under Rule 16.3 include illness or disability, location, parenting leave or unemployment, part-time or casual work, not engaged in legal practice, over 40 years in practice not as principal, and hardship
Pro rata table: April 10 units down to January 1 unit, February and March 0; compulsory fields must still be covered (Rule 6.2)
The CPD Rules for solicitors and barristers are Uniform Rules made by the Legal Services Council
